story_type: 600-foot lava fountain seen from a helicopter
hook: This lava fountain shot over 600 feet into the air.
narration: This fountain of lava shot more than six hundred feet into the air.
This was the summit of Kilauea, Hawaii, on April twenty-second, 2025, episode eighteen of an eruption that began in December.
That is about twice the height of the Statue of Liberty, pedestal and all.
Gas in the magma expands as it rises, like a shaken soda bottle, and hurls the lava skyward.
In about ten hours it poured out roughly five million cubic meters of lava, enough to fill two thousand Olympic pools.
outcome: Then at 1:28 that afternoon both vents stopped almost together, and episode eighteen was over.

location_card.place: Kilauea summit, Hawaii Volcanoes National Park

title: Lava fountain twice the Statue of Liberty
description:
On April 22, 2025, a USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory helicopter overflight filmed high fountaining from the south vent at the summit of Kilauea during episode 18 of the eruption. The fountaining lasted about 10 hours and ended abruptly that afternoon.

Footage: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory video by H. Winslow and M. Patrick, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:April_22,_2025_%E2%80%94_K%C4%ABlauea_Episode_18_Lava_Fountaining_Video.webm

facts.claim: USGS HVO helicopter overflight, April 22, high fountaining from the south vent, Kilauea summit, episode 18
facts.source_quote: This video shows a clip from a USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory monitoring helicopter overflight on Tuesday, April 22, when high fountaining was occurring from the south vent at the summit of Kīlauea during episode 18 of the ongoing eruption.
Lava erupted from both vents with maximum fountains from the south vent reaching over 600 feet (200 meters) high

facts.claim: Fountaining lasted about 10 hours; about 5 million cubic meters erupted
facts.source_quote: The fountaining phase of episode 18 began at 3:20 a.m. this morning and lasted for 10 hours and 8 minutes.
Approximately 5 million cubic meters were erupted at about 140 cubic meters per second.

facts.claim: Outcome: ended abruptly at 1:28 p.m., both vents stopped together
facts.source_quote: ended abruptly at 1:28 p.m. HST on April 22. The north and south vents stopped erupting at approximately the same time.
Each episode of Halemaʻumaʻu lava fountaining since December 23, 2024

extra_sources.excerpt: Episode 18 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended abruptly at 1:28 p.m. HST on April 22. The north and south vents stopped erupting at approximately the same time. The fountaining phase of episode 18 began at 3:20 a.m. this morning and lasted for 10 hours and 8 minutes. Lava erupted from both vents with maximum fountains from the south vent reaching over 600 feet (200 meters) high while those from the north vent remained below 200 feet (60 meters high). Approximately 5 million cubic meters were erupted at about 140 cubic meters per second.
Each episode of Halemaʻumaʻu lava fountaining since December 23, 2024, has continued for 13 hours to 8 days
